### Observed differences

- Activity A01 was not observed at all in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces); in the later window it occurs exactly once in every trace (200 of 200, mean 1.0 occurrence per trace). [OCC001]
- In the earlier window, A16 occurred in every trace but no outgoing transition from A16 was ever observed; in the later window, every observed outgoing transition of A16 (200 of 200) leads to A01. [DIR001, POS002]
- In the earlier window, A16 was always the last event of a trace (relative position 1.0 in all 200 traces); in the later window its mean relative position is about 0.92 with slight variation, so it is no longer last. [POS002]
- In the later window, A01 always sits at the end of the trace (relative position 1.0 with no variation, in all 200 traces). [POS001]
- Earlier, A16 occurred without A01 in all 200 traces (co-occurrence in 0 of 100 cases); later, both activities occur together in every trace, with A16 before A01 in all 200. [REL001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A01 now runs as a new final step, executed once per case immediately after A16, whereas earlier traces ended with A16 and A01 was not observed. In the earlier window A16 was present in every trace, always in the last position, and never followed by another activity; in the later window A01 appears exactly once per trace, always as A16's successor and at the end of the trace, while A16 shifts from last to second-to-last position. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001, POS002, REL001]

Five items qualified against roughly 0.12 expected by chance for the 25 tested control-flow units, so the set of items is far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces, and each difference is larger than in essentially all random re-splits (strength about 0.995). The items agree across participation, routing, position and relation, and the ordering claim rests on direct relational evidence (A16 before A01 in all later traces, A16's only observed successor being A01) rather than on position alone. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001, POS002, REL001]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out: zero participation in the earlier window only shows A01 was not observed there, so A01 may have existed as a rare activity (too rare to appear in 200 traces) that became frequent, and a renaming of an existing activity cannot be excluded. [OCC001]

Other differences: none — the small backward shift of A16's position is a consequence of A01 now following it, not an independent change. [POS002]

Hmm, but POS002 shows A16 present in before window with support 200. So A16 occurs in every before trace but has no observed outgoing transitions? That would mean A16 is always the last activity in before traces. Interesting.

Wait — DIR support is "outgoing transitions of the source activity for DIR". Before: 0 outgoing transitions observed. A16 occurs in all 200 before traces (POS002 support before = 1.0). So A16 never has a successor in the before window — it's the final activity. In the after window, A16 has 200 outgoing transitions, all to A01. So A01 was inserted after A16.

3. POS001: A01 position. Before: support 0 (not observed). After: support 1.0, mean position 1.0 (normalized position presumably, 0 = start, 1 = end?). Mean 1.0, std 0.
